final_candidates.decision_summary: Arg157 lies in the N-terminal catalytic/FAD-binding domain; a proline substitution likely breaks local secondary structure and cofactor coordination, causing severe loss of function.
Removing a large aromatic residue from the catalytic core likely destabilizes the FAD-binding pocket and catalytic geometry, though it may act partly through folding defects.

stop_reason.detail: LLM-only condition provides no new evidence; Top-3 reasoning is stable across self-review.

history.rationale: Known thermolabile polymorphism that destabilizes the catalytic domain and strongly reduces activity; likely insufficient alone to fully abolish function.
Known C677T (A222V) thermolabile variant reduces MTHFR activity substantially in vivo; however it is hypomorphic, not fully abolishing, so confidence stays moderate.
Arg157 lies in the conserved catalytic-core region near substrate binding; proline substitution likely disrupts fold and abolishes catalysis.
R157 sits in the FAD-binding N-terminal catalytic domain; Pro substitution likely disrupts local structure and cofactor binding, plausibly abolishing activity.
Conserved acidic residue in the catalytic N-terminal domain; removal likely impairs chemistry or FAD-dependent electron transfer.
Conserved Asp in the catalytic domain region; loss of acidic side chain may impair substrate binding/catalysis, but catalytic role is uncertain.
Buried tryptophan likely important for hydrophobic core packing; Ala mutation likely causes loss of folded, active enzyme.
Large aromatic-to-alanine change in catalytic domain core likely destabilizes FAD binding pocket; risk is folding rather than clean catalytic loss.
